newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares up across the board.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares up across the board.

text.p: Israeli shares closed up nearly across the board on Sunday with exception of Israel Chemical and Israel Corp, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.38 percent percent, or 3.52 points, to 259.40, on an all-share turnover of 115.6 million shekels against 99 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed +1.2 percent higher at 268.9.

"The market opened with surplus demand which gave the market one direction," said Ilan Doron of Solid Capital Markets. "All the shares rose except those of Israel Chemical and the Israel Corp because investors prefer to get out until it is clear who will run the company," he said.

The Israel Corp closed down 6.25 percent to 20,936 agorot and Israel Chemicals closed down 3.00 percent to 404 agorot on media reports that the company would lie at the centre of a burgeoning family fued for control of the international empire of the late billionaire Shoul Eisenberg.
The Israel Corp holds 41.9 in Israel Chemicals.
Israel Corp is one of Israel's major holding companies with investments in over 80 leading companies. Company founder Shoul Eisenberg died of a heart attack in Beijing in March.

"A few things pushed the market up today," said Doron. "Trading in the banks pushed the market up, because of their privatisation plans and because foreign investors are buying their shares on the market. The rises in Wall Street also affected the market as well as talks about Israel and the Palestinians renewing in some way the peace talks."
"The market was waiting for a positive momentum on the political front to give itself a push," he said.
Israel and the Palestinians set a high-level meeting on Tuesday to try and save the deadlocked peace process.
Peacemaking between Israel and the Palestinians ground to a halt in March when Israel began building a 6,500-unit Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Shares in Israel Discount Bank rose 3.75 percent to 366 agorot on a very high turnover of 12.3 million shekels. "There is a fight over the control of the bank. Someone is buying up shares in the company to control the bank," said Gidi Halpern at Meitav Investments and Securities.

Teva rose 3.25 percent to 17,899 on volume of 5.2 million shekels on the gains in Wall Street. Teva said on Sunday that it had received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to manufacture and market Trazodone 150 mg tablets.
Another highly traded stock was Koor, which rose 2.0 percent to 30,165 agorot on volume of 4.8 million shekels.
